content.text:
The drawing shows a 3-chlorophenyl ring joined to a central CH carbon. That carbon carries an NO2 group and a sulfonyl group (S with two =O). The sulfur is bonded to a p-tolyl ring.

Checking the chlorine position: the ring attachment point is at the lower right of the ring, and the Cl sits at the top vertex. Going from the attachment carbon to the upper-right vertex and then to the top vertex puts Cl two atoms away, so it is meta, which matches 3-chlorophenyl.

The central carbon is a stereocentre by connectivity, but it is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereo is given.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(cc1)S(=O)(=O)C([N+](=O)[O-])c1cccc(Cl)c1
